'''Janos Kirz''' (born 1937) is a Hungarian-American [[physicist]], [[professor emeritus]] at [[Stony Brook University]], and pioneer of [[Soft X-ray microscopy|X-ray microscopy]].<ref name="SBProfile">{{cite web|url=https://www.stonybrook.edu/commcms/physics/people/_profiles/kirzj|title=Janos Kirz|publisher=Stony Brook University Department of Physics and Astronomy|accessdate=October 18, 2025}}</ref><ref name="sloan"/>

==Biography==
Born in [[Budapest, Hungary]], Kirz emigrated to the United States in late 1956 after the [[Hungarian Revolution of 1956]]. Kirz earned a [[Bachelor of Arts]] in [[physics]] from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1959 and received his PhD in physics from the same institution in 1963. He then spent 1963–1964 as a [[postdoctoral fellow]] at the [[French Atomic Energy Commission]] (Commissariat à l’énergie atomique et aux énergies alternatives) in [[Saclay]]. In 1968 Kirz took a position at [[Stony Brook University]] where he was appointed professor in 1973.<ref>
{{cite web
 |url=http://www-als.lbl.gov/index.php/ring-leaders/665-janos-kirz.html
 |title=Janos Kirz
 |publisher=Advanced Light Source, [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]]
 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304101757/http://www-als.lbl.gov/index.php/ring-leaders/665-janos-kirz.html
 |archive-date=2016-03-04
 |access-date=2022-06-22}}
</ref>
Kirz is the nephew of physicist [[Edward Teller]].
<ref>
{{cite web
 |url=https://www.llnl.gov/news/symposium-reviews-edward-teller%E2%80%99s-varied-contributions-science
 |title=Symposium reviews Edward Teller's varied contributions to science}}
</ref>
<ref>
{{cite book |last=Hargittai |first=István |author-link= |date=2006 |title=Martians of Science: Five Physicists Who Changed the Twentieth Century |url=https://global.oup.com/academic/product/martians-of-science-9780195365566 |location=United Kingdom |publisher=Oxford University Press |page=10 |isbn= 9780199884414}}
</ref>

==Research==
Kirz’s research centers on the development of [[soft X-ray microscopy]] techniques using [[Fresnel zone]] plates and the application of these methods to biological and materials science investigations.

* 2005 - Arthur H. Compton Award from the [[Advanced Photon Source]] for "Pioneering and developing the field of x-ray microscopy using Fresnel zone plates".
